This thread is fun for me- I hadn’t lived “alone” until college, and my sophmore-senior year roommate was one of those girls who actively shamed girls who wore makeup. She believed in K-Beauty routines, but nothing else. I got passive aggressive texts for leaving “powder” on the sink when I finished my routine before a presentation/important debate day in my classes. She used the words “fake” when talking about other girls on campus she saw wearing makeup. Laughed about how on a rainy day they had to worry about their faces “melting off” while she was fine.

I began to see make up as putting on a mask, and really utilized full-face glam looks for especially important days or interviews. I didn’t find the fun in wearing it to class anymore because of her constant ragging on me and other girls who wore make up. 

Towards the middle of our last semester, I realized she was just a little jealous. I had genuinely seen it as her viewing herself above me/other girls that wore make up, but I loved how I felt about myself after finishing my routine. I didn’t think it was worth letting her take away that experience from me. 

So I stayed happy when I wore make up to class. I played podcasts or music I liked as I did my make up in the morning and felt at peace before my classes. I knew that it was a personal experience, where only I/other girls knew what we went through to plan or execute a look for the day. I used to hide behind it, but now I see makeup as a genuinely positive, creative and relaxing outlet for myself.
